sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Köln's parking policy has two parts: residents' permits, where the city has acted, and the general fee ordinance, where it has not. Residents' permits rose from 30 to 100 euros a year on 1 October 2024; from 1 March 2025 the fee is tiered by vehicle length at 100, 110 and 120 euros, and owners of vehicles over 5,600 mm generally no longer have a right to a permit, according to the city's statement of September 2024 [9]. That followed a November 2023 proposal, made after the city withdrew a May 2023 proposal of 330 to 390 euros; at that time Köln had 47 residents' parking zones with about 51,400 spaces and 61,020 permits, and the city assumed about 20 percent fewer permits [6]. We found no 2026 source that confirms the tiers are unchanged.

The general Parkgebührenordnung is stuck. In November 2024 the administration proposed raising short-term parking from 4 to 5 euros an hour in the Innenstadt and Deutz and from 2 to 2.50 euros elsewhere, setting long-term parking at 30 euros a day and ending long-term parking inside the Kölner Ringe, with a council decision planned for February 2025 [10]. The council postponed the decision on 27 May 2025 [11], and on 9 September 2026 t-online Köln reported that there is still no decision; a city spokeswoman said the draft has been before the council since 13 February 2025, and the paper itself said it had not been on the agenda since the municipal election [16]. These are proposals, not rules. The fee conversion of 2020, when the city started changing its roughly 2,750 meters to 1 euro per started 15 minutes in the centre, was the last increase [0]. Around the Dom, a package of temporary changes on Trankgasse in spring 2023 created a car-free area and bicycle streets; the IHK assesses the redesign critically and the Tiefgarage am Dom exit remains reachable through a release for motor traffic [4]. In 2022 the city trialled a pedestrian zone on the Deutzer Freiheit, converting some parking spaces [1].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The most visible event is the closure of the Tiefgarage Groß St. Martin. It was closed to the public with immediate effect on 15 September 2025 for structural investigations of about 50 concrete columns, with no reopening date given; the city named Am Dom, Philharmonie, An Farina, Hauptbahnhof and Heumarkt as alternatives [13]. On 16 December 2025 the council decided to raise fees in the city's garages to an average hourly rate of 2.10 euros, up from 1.44 euros: for example Breslauer Platz rises from 0.60 to 0.80 euro per started 20 minutes with the daily maximum going from 18 to 24 euros, while Am Dom stays at 0.80 euro and 24 euros. The city planned the new rates for 1 February 2026, but the page does not confirm that they started [15].

Private operators have expanded: Q-Park took over the Barthonia Forum in Ehrenfeld, with 1,043 spaces, from 1 May 2024 [8], and announced a new management contract for the I/D Cologne garage in Mülheim, with 896 spaces and 24 charging stations, in 2023 [5]. On park and ride, the city plans a Parkpalette at Weiden-West with about 130 bicycle boxes and over 200 bicycle stands in place of 66 car spaces [12]. In 2022 the city signed a contract with Stadtwerke Köln for 1,000 further public charging points, with the 1,000th planned for 2026 [3].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The city's Parkleitsystem connected garages with more than 20,000 spaces in 2022 [2] and 22,000 spaces in 2025, with 27 variable-message boards on the access roads [14]. The system is used for event traffic. After the first three Advent weekends of 2023 the city said its concept had worked: about 722 coaches used the Koelnmesse P22 car park with a shuttle, and the Lanxess-Arena and Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring garages were well used, with queues in front of full garages [7]. For Advent 2025 the city made the parking tickets of the Lanxess-Arena and Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring garages valid as group day tickets on buses and trains [14].

Our listing has 50 garages with about 19,600 spaces, of which four operators hold most: Contipark with 24 garages and about 6,700 spaces (median hourly rate 4.35 euros), Kalscheuer Parkhausbetriebe with 11 and 5,700 (3.00 euros), APCOA with 9 and 3,900 (2.00 euros) and Q-Park with 6 and 3,300 (2.25 euros). Köln's measured data are too new to describe a pattern. We receive readings from the Mobilithek (the national mobility data platform), started on 15 to 19 October 2026 for the first garages, and by 21 October we had three weekdays for 29 garages with 13,178 spaces. On those days, weighted by spaces, they averaged 43%; without the Lanxess arena garages and Ring Karree, which sat at full on a Monday noon and may reflect an event or a counter fault, 37%. A legacy city feed with other capacities covers only 28 to 30 September, so we do not combine the two. Treat these figures as a first look rather than a profile.
